## Verified Product And Data Decisions

- The first complete product path is: coach invites by email -> invitee activates account -> coach assigns and publishes a personalized routine -> student signs in and completes it.
- Initial product scope is personalized training only. Every coach/member account and member-gym relationship enters by invitation; public self-signup, bulk/group registration, group-class scheduling, booking, attendance, and per-class capacity are deferred until the personalized MVP is complete.
- `tenants.max_clients` remains a tenant setting for future use, but is not enforced for invite-only personalized memberships. These sessions do not reserve class seats or member-capacity slots; invitation, acceptance, and reactivation do not check `max_clients`. Revisit limits only if a future product service explicitly requires them.
- CU-01B email invitations are onboarding to a persistent gym membership, not reservations for classes. Personalized training is programmed by the coach for the user; group-class booking remains deferred.
- Coach roster email is read from `auth.users` only through `list_coach_personalized_members()`, which derives the coach from `auth.uid()` and returns only same-tenant personalized members linked to that coach. Do not query or expose `auth.users` directly to the client.
- Per-member routines and daily workout completion are not persisted yet; coach roster cards must say there is no active programming rather than display demo progress from another user.
- Current invitation onboarding creates only personalized members. Do not design or expose group-only, dual-service, or mass-registration flows during this phase. Revisit service entitlements and unique-member capacity accounting only when group services are explicitly brought into scope.
- `supabase/functions/invite-personalized-member/index.ts` verifies the bearer session, derives the active coach and tenant from `profiles`, calls the service-only prepare RPC, sends Auth invite/recovery email, links newly invited Auth identities, and marks an unlinked invitation failed if Auth did not create an identity. Local HTTP checks returned `sent`, then `resent`, kept one pending invitation, captured both emails in Mailpit, and rejected a request without a session with 401. Temporary coach/invitee records and only their Mailpit messages were removed.
- `supabase/functions/accept-personalized-invitation/index.ts` validates the signed-in invitee and delegates atomic profile activation to the acceptance RPC. Coach UI invokes the invite endpoint; the email destination opens the invitee completion screen, which verifies the email-backed session, sets a password (minimum 10 characters), submits full name, accepts the invitation, removes the invitation query parameter, and reloads the active profile. Browser verification confirmed the member could sign out and sign back in with the new password. Demo student routines, metrics, and coach details remain mock data; a newly invited member must not mistake them for assigned/persisted programming, and CU-03/CU-04 should replace them with a truthful no-programming state and real data.
- Membership is granted only through the coach invitation flow; public self-signup remains disabled. Existing active personalized members are intentionally rejected as duplicate invitations (`member_already_exists`), and an unexpired pending invitation is reused. Account attachment by email for identities created outside this invite-only flow is not part of the current product scope; do not treat it as a pending requirement.
- Invitation links expire automatically after one hour; the backend marks an unused pending invitation `EXPIRED` when it is next checked. Expiry does not reserve or release class/member capacity because personalized memberships have no seat limit. A coach-facing manual cancellation action is out of scope. Member inactivation is a separate lifecycle action after acceptance.
- Coach/member visibility invariant: an authenticated member may read only their own profile; an active coach may read only accepted personalized-member profiles whose `coach_id` equals that coach's `auth.uid()`, and the composite FK keeps both in the same gym; `super_admin` retains platform-wide access. Migration 007 enforces this policy locally and in Production. pgTAP verifies isolation between two coaches in one gym. Pending invitation records remain private to trusted server code unless a separate coach-scoped view is deliberately designed.
- Migration 006 sets invitation link lifetime to one hour, matching the current one-hour Auth OTP lifetime. Supabase Auth verification tokens are single-use; acceptance transitions the invitation from `PENDING` to `ACCEPTED`, and a repeated acceptance request now fails with `invitation_not_pending`. Expired, unaccepted linked invitations can be reissued to the same Auth identity with a fresh recovery link; no class/member capacity is reserved. Email is normalized and checked against the signed-in Auth user's email both when linking the Auth identity and again during acceptance. Accepted member profiles persist `coach_id=tenant_invitations.invited_by`, and a composite FK guarantees coach and member share the same tenant.
- Implemented in migrations 003/004/010: the tenant row is locked during invitation/onboarding operations; same-tenant pending invitations are reused; expired onboarding can be reissued; accepted invitations atomically create the active profile. Personalized invitations and reactivation do not enforce class/member capacity. Inactive profiles retain their identity/history but lose tenant access; the coach can reactivate them through a confirmed toggle.
- Public self-signup stays disabled. A browser must never choose its role or `tenant_id`, and service-role credentials must never reach Vite/client code.
- The full Exercise contract is: `id`, `name`, `series`, `reps`, `weight`, optional `workDuration`, `rest`, `emoji`, `muscles`, `instructions`, `tips`, `difficulty`, optional `videoUrl`. Preserve every field through library -> assignment snapshot -> student execution. Keep assignment overrides separate from catalog defaults. Video is optional today; validate its reference and show an explicit no-video state.
- The coach roster, dashboard member summary/recent list, and coach profile member count load persisted invitee profiles through `coachMemberRepository`; member emails use the authenticated coach-scoped RPC. The dashboard recent list and student list show email, account status, and a truthful no-active-programming label, with the shared compact pink status toggle. CU-02's coach exercise library now reads Supabase directly, with no silent mock fallback; routine editing remains mock/localStorage-backed and student check-offs remain in component state.
- Keep an explicit `mock` or `supabase` data mode behind typed repositories. Do not mix sources or silently fall back to mocks on database errors. Mocks remain useful for tests/demo while each vertical slice is moved and verified against local Supabase.
- Local catalog seeds may persist stable-ID demonstration exercises idempotently after schema/RLS is ready. They are demo fixtures, not real user data. Do not seed fake Auth users or personal data in SQL; provision local identities with development-only scripts.
- Existing samples use generic YouTube URLs; do not present them as valid instructional videos. Decide approved external HTTPS URLs versus Supabase Storage when implementing CU-02, then validate/play the chosen format.
- Templates are optional for the first direct student/date assignment. Offline sync is deferred; the first execution flow is online and persists workout/session data.
- Current localhost defaults to tenant `ags`, so it cannot exercise a tenant-less `super_admin` platform context without a separate host setup.
- Vercel configuration uses `VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://vmrcwizgluzvsmmkkhnt.supabase.co`, the project's publishable/anon key, `VITE_ROOT_DOMAIN=tugimnasioapp.com`, `VITE_DEFAULT_TENANT_SUBDOMAIN=ags`, and `VITE_PREVIEW_TENANT_HOSTNAME=ags-roan-iota.vercel.app`. Do not place service-role or secret keys in Vercel frontend variables. Hosted schema, tenant, coach profile, Auth redirect, invitation functions, and personal Gmail SMTP are configured.

## Required Status-Update Task

At the end of every implementation or documentation change, update this snapshot in the same work item:

- Mark any touched use case as implemented, partial, blocked, or planned based on verified evidence.
- Record schema, security, seed, test, or configuration changes and validation results.
- Refresh the immediate next step if dependencies or decisions changed.
- Keep the distinction between committed implementation and local uncommitted changes accurate.
- If no project status changed, explicitly state that the status was reviewed and remains accurate; do not add noise-only edits.
